messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: elevated 5xx rate observed from the gateway to user-facing APIs. Trigger threshold 3.5% -> currently 9.8% over last 3m. Affected endpoints: /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings. Suspected upstream: auth-service org-lookup/billing calls failing. Pager: @oncall-nights

irene: acked, on it. any customer-impact details?

sam: seeing 502 and some 504s at the gateway. Spikes align with a sharp increase in requests to /auth/validate-token and /org/lookup. Error logs show 500 from auth with `KeyError('token_cache')` around the same time.

manny: adding logs from gateway + auth: ```
gateway: [2026-03-15T02:45:21Z] upstream auth-service 502 "Bad gateway" for /v1/chat (reqid=xyz)
auth: [2026-03-15T02:45:20Z] ERROR validate_token failed for token id=abc123 exc=KeyError('token_cache') stack=...
org-lookup: [2026-03-15T02:45:20Z] WARN timeout contacting billing (50ms -> 6000ms)
```

jia: note: we rolled cached token invalidation change last night (rollout=50%) — could be traffic pattern + rollout exposing race in cache invalidation code.

leo: customer impact: some high-traffic tenants on us-east-1 reporting intermittent 502s. SLAs: P2 but trending P1 if sustained. ETA to mitigation?

irene: short mitigation plan: 1) pause rollout of cache-invalidation flag 2) bump auth replicas 3) enable fallback read-only org cache for org-lookup 4) route a small percentage of traffic to fallback model. Doing 1 and 2 now.

sam: running rollout rollback: ```
kubectl -n infra set env deployment/auth-service CACHE_INVALIDATION_ROLLOUT=0 --record
kubectl -n infra scale deployment/auth-service --replicas=6
```

ops-bot: deploy event recorded by deploy-bot: rollback env update for auth-service by sam at 2026-03-15T02:47:10Z

manny: after rollback, auth error rate dropped from 16% -> 6% in 45s, but gateway still seeing 5xx (~6%). Likely downstream org/billing timeout fanout.

jia: enabling read-only org cache and raising org-lookup timeout to 2s (was 800ms): ```
# feature flags
ORG_LOOKUP_READ_ONLY_CACHE=true
ORG_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT_MS=2000
```

leo: note to SRE: can we temporarily increase circuit-breaker thresholds for gateway->auth to prevent immediate 5xx cascades? Would like to reduce fail-open frequency.

irene: yes. setting cb thresholds and adding a short-lived traffic shaping rule to limit request bursts to auth to 600 rps.

sam: cb change applied. Also added a KV cache warmup job for tokens to reduce cold misses. Watching metrics.

incidents-bot: incident severity elevated to P1 (when customer error rate >8% for >5m). Current 3m average down to 3.2% after mitigations. Notable tenants XCorp and FinApp saw spikes earlier but are now mostly recovered.

manny: still seeing occasional 502s tied to billing call latency. We should consider a temporary static response or graceful degradation when billing times out (return soft-allowed responses instead of hard 5xx).

irene: agree. putting a graceful-degrade middleware behind a feature flag for billing calls. Code snippet for fallback: ```python
def get_org_billing(org_id):
    try:
        return billing_api.get(org_id, timeout=2.0)
    except TimeoutError:
        # fall back to last-known-good or minimal billing object
        return {
            "plan": "unknown",
            "limits": default_limits
        }
```

oncall-nights: taking handoff for overnight monitoring. irene, sam — leaving runbook steps and contact list.

irene: handoff notes -> runbook entries: actions taken, rollback of cache flag, scaled auth to 6, org-cache read-only enabled, CB thresholds increased, billing degrade flag enabled (feature flag = true). If errors climb back above 5% for >3m, page infra-leads and open incident channel.

sam: added dashboards: token-cache-miss-rate, auth-500-rate, org-lookup-latency, gateway-5xx. Alert thresholds adjusted for burst windows.

leo: customer comms: preparing a short note for affected tenants: "We observed elevated 5xx errors between 02:43–02:50 UTC due to an auth cache invalidation regression. We rolled back the change and applied mitigations. If you still see errors, please DM support." Draft sent to comms channel.

manny: postmortem pointers: isolate the cache invalidation rollout path, add a canary test that simulates token churn, add a circuit-breaker graceful degrade for billing, and increase observability on token-cache metrics.

incidents-bot: all clear check scheduled in 30m. Please update the incident document with timeline and customer impact when stable. :white_check_mark:

oncall-nights: ack. Leaving monitoring in place, will escalate if anything reappears.

irene: thanks team. Will open post-incident ticket for rollback validation + stricter rollout gating.

sam: one last note — we saw a small spike in retries from downstream clients which contributed to the burst. Recommend adding jitter to client retry logic in sdk clients.

manny: logging snippet saved to s3://redwood-incidents/2987654321/logs.txt for later analysis.

incidents-bot: incident channel archived (soft) when severity stable for 30m.
